cairo_layout sets text as a picture, for a screen or projector rather than the patch.

WHY NOT text_display:
text_display is for you, while you work. This is for an audience. It renders through Cairo into an image, so the result goes to a projector, a texture, or anything else that takes a picture - in a font you chose, at a size you chose.

The 'layout' outlet is that image: 1920 by 1080 unless the node is given
another size (cairo_layout <width> <height>), three channels, as floats from
0 to 1 - laid out height-first like a camera frame rather than channels-first. So it goes straight into the same places a camera picture does. The text is white on black.

TWO INLETS, TWO JOBS:
'input' REPLACES: each text that arrives clears the picture and sets the new text. 'command' builds up and edits:

add <words>        append words to what is there
add_char <c>       append one character, with no space before it
delete_line        remove back to the last line break
clear / reset      empty it
scroll_up / scroll_down   move active_line by one
save               write the text to llama_output_<date>.txt in the
                   folder the app was started from

Inside the text, \n is a line break, a word \c clears the picture and a word \d deletes back to the last line break.

'active_line' IS WHERE THE TEXT ENDS:
The last line of the text sits on line 'active_line' of the picture (counting lines of 'leading' from the top), and everything earlier is above it - lines pushed off the top are not drawn. Set it low and you see only the end of a long text; set it near the bottom and the text fills the picture as it grows.

A new node starts at line 17, which with the default leading of 60 puts the last line near the foot of a 1080-high picture. Changing active_line moves what is already shown straight away, by exactly the change.

THE TYPE:
'font path' takes a font file. Empty uses the Inconsolata font that comes with the app; a path that cannot be loaded falls back to Cairo's own default, so a missing font never stops the node working - it just looks wrong, which is easier to diagnose than a crash.

'leading' is the distance between lines in pixels - line spacing, not letter spacing. Changing 'font size' resets it to one and a half times the size, so set the size first.

'wrap text' folds long lines to the width instead of letting them run off.

BRIGHTNESS PER WORD:
A word can arrive with a weight from 0 to 1, as a [word, weight] pair in a list. Its grey level is the weight raised to 'alpha power', times 'brightness'. Plain words have weight 1, so for them only 'brightness' matters. 'alpha power' shapes the falloff: at 1 a weight of 0.1 is a dark grey, at the default 0.1 it is nearly as bright as the rest. A word of weight 0 is left out.

SYNTAX:
cairo_layout <width> <height>

EXAMPLE:
cairo_layout

INPUTS and PARAMETERS:

input:
Text to show, replacing what was there.

command:
The commands above.

clear:
Empty it.

font path / font size:
The typeface and its size (40).

brightness / alpha power:
The grey level of the text, and how word weights map to it.

leading:
Line spacing, 60.

active_line:
The line the text ends on (17).

wrap text:
Fold long lines to the width.

OUTPUTS:

layout:
The rendered image.

RELATED:
llm_layout, the same idea built for a language model's output; it used to share this page. text_display to read text inside the patch instead. mgl_texture or gl nodes to get the image onto a screen.
